nodes.description: The standard regimen for drug-susceptible tuberculosis: isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for two months, then isoniazid and rifampicin for four months. Three randomized trials in intestinal and peritoneal tuberculosis found six months as effective as nine, and an older trial found a six-month rifampicin-isoniazid-pyrazinamide regimen as effective as twelve months of ethambutol and isoniazid with initial streptomycin. The trials excluded people with HIV and comorbidities. Drug absorption may be impaired with extensive small-bowel disease, so persistent symptoms beyond about two weeks should prompt consideration of complications, malabsorption, drug resistance or another diagnosis. Adverse effects occurred in about a fifth of trial patients.
